problem: Step 8 says 'The endurance limit is 400 MPa, half of 800 MPa.' Stating the fraction invites students to use Se = Su/2 as a rule, which the exam traps then tell them not to do. The sentence pulls against the trap.
fix: The test data level off at 400 MPa, so Se = 400 MPa. Here that happens to be half the ultimate strength of 800 MPa, but do not generalise this; take the endurance limit from test data or a design code.

problem: The lead says 500 MPa repeated 'ten thousand times' can grow a crack until the part breaks. The worked example gives the life at 500 MPa as about 22,300 cycles, so 10,000 cycles would not break this part. The two numbers contradict each other.
fix: Say the part fails at about 22,000 cycles at 500 MPa, or drop the specific cycle count in the lead: 'the same stress repeated tens of thousands of times can start a crack and grow it until the part breaks.'

problem: The S-N curve is only valid for a fully reversed cycle (mean stress zero, R = −1), which is what rotating bending gives. The chapter never states this baseline condition, though it later says mean stress changes the result.
fix: Add one line: 'The S-N curve from rotating bending is for a fully reversed cycle, tension and compression equal, mean stress zero. Other mean stresses shift the curve.'

problem: The flat 400 MPa endurance-limit line is drawn from 10³ cycles onwards, so it overlaps the whole life range even though the data only become horizontal at 10⁶ cycles. A student may read it as 'endurance limit applies from 10³'.
fix: Draw the sloping line from 10³ to 10⁶ cycles and draw the flat endurance-limit line only from 10⁶ cycles onward, or label it 'applies beyond 10⁶ cycles'.
